selected.rationale: The near-black interface uses one strong left-side information block, restrained navigation, compact metrics, generous negative space, and quiet off-white typography; borrow its disciplined dark framing and hierarchy for the floating graphite route composer, not its landing-page content.

The softly lit mint, blue-gray, dusty rose, and off-white environment provides the most relevant low-saturation alpine color balance and diffuse material softness for a warm map under graphite glass; do not borrow the office subject.

The precise axonometric line studies on alternating light and dark fields support restrained terrain-layer symbols, map utilities, and technical route geometry without introducing decorative pictograms.

The spacious white principles sheet uses sparse circular diagrams, short captions, consistent spacing, and clear grouping; translate that economy into compact score/status chips and a low-profile task surface over the map.

rejected.reason: The nearly blank pale interface has too little contrast and recoverable component detail at preview size to guide a variable-luminance map UI.
The centered radial pattern and circular hero are ornamental and page-like rather than useful for a focused route-composer overlay.
The dense dark code/document page offers weak spatial guidance for a lightweight map-first application.
This second dense code/document screen duplicates the same text-heavy territory and would encourage dashboard density.
The red-green cyberpunk terminal palette conflicts with the accepted warm Paper, Graphite, Alpine Mint, and Route Blue system.
The branded campaign photograph with large overlaid copy is not relevant to an implementable map interface and introduces avoidable trademark risk.
The saturated wildlife campaign image and display copy are visually dominant but unrelated to route planning, hierarchy, or translucent controls.
The branded lifestyle campaign crop and overlaid text would pull the result toward advertising rather than a restrained desktop tool.
